plan:
FULL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "Do SPAG's adversarial Taboo self-play reasoning gains exceed non-adversarial game setups?"

0) PRE-REGISTERED ENDPOINT PRECEDENCE (declared a priori)
- PRIMARY: pre→post Δ on held-out reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K, StrategyQA, HotpotQA, ASDiv, last-letter, coin-flip). Chosen because it measures transfer of general reasoning, not game-specific skill.
- SECONDARY (descriptive only, never a substitute for primary): in-game win-rate against frozen adversaries, because it can reward game-specific exploits.
- A model "improves reasoning over" another iff its primary Δ is larger with statistical support (Section 6). No analysis of the secondary endpoint may veto the primary conclusion.

1) ARMS TABLE (5 arms; only the game/curriculum differs)
| Arm | Curriculum | Pipeline | Seeds | Purpose |
|----|-----------|----------|-------|---------|
| A | Adversarial Taboo | GPT-4-IL → self-play → DPO | 5 (a priori {0..4}) | Target: SPAG adversarial setup (setup_32) |
| B | 20-Question (cooperative) | same pipeline | 5 | Non-adversarial comparator (setup_33) |
| C | Guess-My-City (cooperative) | same pipeline | 5 | Non-adversarial comparator (setup_33) |
| D | Taboo imitation-only | GPT-4-IL, NO self-play/DPO | 3 (5 if budget allows) | Isolates self-play gain (A−D) |
| E | Generic instruction (token-matched) | SFT only, no game | 3 (5 if budget allows) | Isolates data-volume/instruction gain (A−E) |

Rationale: A vs B vs C answers the headline question; D and E make causal attribution defensible — Δ(A) must exceed both Δ(B) and Δ(C) (adversarial factor) AND Δ(D) (self-play, not just SFT) AND Δ(E) (data volume, not just more finetuning). A/B/C each need both DPO and self-play so arm differences are clean. D/E skip DPO by design and cost less.

2) PIPELINE PER GAME ARM (A, B, C) — single dual-role student
Stage 1 — Imitation learning (IL): GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613, temperature 0.7) plays T=1,000 games per seed of the arm's game, producing full trajectories (role-labeled utterances). SFT the student on all role-conditioned utterances. D and E receive the same token budget of teacher data (D: Taboo trajectories without self-play; E: instruction data).
Stage 2 — Self-play (adversarial for A; cooperative self-rollout for B/C): the SFT student plays the SAME game against itself, roles assigned per episode; for A the partner samples with temperature 1.0 (adversarial diversity), for B/C same rollout scheme. Collect 50k episodes/arm with win/lose outcome.
Stage 3 — DPO: preference pairs (chosen = winning trajectories, rejected = losing) under DPO (β=0.1) against the SFT checkpoint as reference.

3) FIXED-ACROSS-ARMS CONTROLS (the whole experiment is the factor "game adversarially")
- Base model: Llama-2-7B-chat, identical HF checkpoint across arms.
- Teacher data volume: token-matched per arm (total SFT tokens equal to ±0.5%).
- Self-play volume: 50k episodes/arm; decoding identical (rollout temp 0.7, top-p 0.95; greedy 0 for eval).
- DPO hyperparameters identical (β, LR, epochs, batch, seq len).
- Seeds: same seed set reused across arms so Δs are paired per seed {0..4}.
- Eval protocol and prompt templates identical; same held-out benchmark splits; same frozen opponent pool for in-game eval.

4) COMMITTED HYPERPARAMETERS (design commitments, not SPAG-verified)
- Model: Llama-2-7B-chat (HF), full-parameter fine-tuning via FSDP/DeepSpeed stage-2.
- SFT: 3 epochs, AdamW, LR 2e-5, cosine schedule, warmup 3%, batch 64, max_seq_len 2048, weight decay 0.1.
- Teacher data: 1,000 GPT-4 games/arm/seed → ~60k SFT examples ≈ ~1.5M tokens/arm (token-matched).
- Self-play: 50k episodes/arm, temperature 1.0 partner / 0.7 self, episode = ≥1 and ≤8 role-turn pairs or target hit, clue ≤30 tokens, guess ≤10 tokens.
- DPO: β=0.1, LR 5e-6, 1 epoch, batch 32, seq 2048, reference = SFT ckpt.
- Taboo config (assumption): target word + 2–3 taboo words; clue must not contain target/taboo words or subwords; hit = guesser names target within budget.
- Eval: GSM8K 8-shot CoT, StrategyQA CoT, HotpotQA (distractor) 2-shot, ASDiv CoT, last-letter & coin-flip few-shot symbolic; greedy, exact-match/pass@1.

5) EVALUATION
- Pre: base model on all benchmarks. Post: each arm×seed on the same splits with same prompts.
- Primary metric per arm: distribution over seeds of Δ = post_mean − pre_mean on a benchmark aggregate (averaged over the six tasks) AND benchmark-wise Δs (reported separately so transfer breadth is visible, never cherry-picked).
- Secondary: Taboo win-rate vs a FROZEN opponent pool (5 fixed Llama-2-7B GPT-4-distilled Taboo players, fixed decoding), 100 held-out Taboo instances × 5 opponents, win-rate per seeded arm (A/B/C only; descriptive, Section 0).

6) ANALYSIS PLAN (per-seed paired, nonparametric)
- Per seed s: Δ_{arm,s}. All contrasts are paired on the same seed set.
- Primary contrasts, declared a priori: H1: Δ_A > Δ_B; H2: Δ_A > Δ_C. Test: one-sided exact permutation/Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-seed Δ pairs; Holm-Bonferroni correction across H1,H2 (α = 0.05).
- Report: mean Δ, SD, 95% CI via seed-resampled bootstrap, and Hedges' g for A-vs-B and A-vs-C (with CIs). Interpret only when H1∧H2 pass with g CI excluding 0.
- Supporting (pre-registered as conditional, not primary): A vs D (self-play ablation) and A vs E (data-volume control) — if either fails, the headline claim is weakened accordingly.
- Diagnostics: self-play win-rate trajectory should plateau (monitor for collapse/cheating); rollout perplexity/diversity tracked; benchmark contamination check = no benchmark train or few-shot exemplar text appears in any training data.

7) FEASIBILITY / GPU-BUDGET NOTE (for a peer with compute; nothing runs here)
- Bottleneck is self-play rollouts: 50k episodes × 2 actors per arm ≈ 100k generation calls/arm. vLLM on 8×A100-80GB ≈ 1–2 days/arm.
- SFT: ~2–4 h/run on 8×A100-80GB (or 8×A100-40GB); DPO ~3–6 h/run.
- Total runs: A/B/C = 15 (SFT+SP+DPO), D = 3 (SFT only), E = 3 (SFT only) → ≈ 2–3 weeks wall-clock on 8×A100-80GB, or ~$5–9k cloud (A100-80GB at ~$2/h). GPT-4 API cost for teacher demos is minor (~$200). All data components are public/open: Llama-2 (HF), GSM8K/StrategyQA/HotpotQA/ASDiv (HF), Taboo wordlists (open sources such as Hugging Face Taboo sets), so the plan is runnable by an unaffiliated peer.

8) ASSUMPTIONS vs FIXED REQUIREMENTS
Fixed task requirements (cannot be modified): design-only, no executed experiment; no compute/network in this environment; endpoint precedence (primary=benchmark Δ, secondary=in-game); seeds 5/5/5/3/3; D and E arms present; identical token budget/decoding/DPO hyperparameters across arms; every unverifiable SPAG detail stays flagged as an assumption — never asserted as fact.
Assumptions (explicitly flagged, unverifiable because /workspace contains no SPAG source, no paper, no code, no datasets, and network is off): (i) SPAG = SFT on GPT-4 Taboo demos → self-play → DPO with single dual-role Llama-2-7B student; (ii) exact Taboo mechanics (wordlist, taboo counts, turn/time limits); (iii) GPT-4 demo prompt templates and sampling (no official template available to us); (iv) DPO reward = win/lose only (no graded score); (v) LR schedules and scale (7B vs 8B-class) as committed above; (vi) benchmark prompt/CoT style; (vii) the entire numeric hyperparameter table in Section 4 is OUR commitment, not a verified SPAG value.

context.question: Does the adversarial game setup used in SPAG, which includes imitation learning of GPT-4 followed by self-play on game episodes (specifically via the adversarial Taboo game), provide superior reasoning improvements compared to non-adversarial setups like 20-Question and Guess-My-City?
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.
